summary: When stance classification ran without an LLM and too few works survived the relevance gate, the guard must blank the VERDICT as well as the EvidenceStrength badge — a directional headline with "insufficient" printed underneath it is read as the directional headline — while ConsensusScore and Confidence stay untouched so the record of which way the thin evidence pointed survives.
reason: Measured keyless on "HPV vaccine causes infertility" (--limit 20): three relevant works, one refuting and two inconclusive, produced consensus_score -1.00 with evidence_guarded already true. The guard downgraded the strength badge to "insufficient" and the run still headlined "evidence-refutes": a perfect refutation manufactured from a single paper. The direction happened to be right, but the certainty was not earned, and the same mechanism produces an equally confident "evidence-supports" whenever a thin lexical corpus leans the other way — which is the vaccines/autism failure the guard was built for in the first place. A badge is a footnote; the verdict is the headline, and only downgrading the footnote leaves the claim standing. Three things a regen must not undo. (1) THE SCORE STAYS. ConsensusScore and Confidence are a reproducible heuristic; blanking them alongside the verdict would destroy the evidence of which way the thin corpus pointed, which is the only diagnostic a reader has left once the labels are gone. (2) THE EARLY RETURNS STAY EXACTLY AS THEY ARE. The llm: method prefix bypasses the guard because an LLM vetted relevance, and the count test is relevantCount >= LowEvidenceThreshold, not >; an off-by-one at that boundary silently neutralises verdicts that are backed by enough evidence to state one. (3) THE PROOF MUST STAY SYNTHETIC. No archived corpus can exercise this path, so a regen that drops the hand-written test loses the only coverage this behavior has.
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... -count=1 all clean across the module. The non-obvious measurement is that this change moves no archived result AND the archived corpora cannot demonstrate it either: all 13 exports in internal/scengine/testdata/corpora_full/ (and the 13 in testdata/corpora/) carry evidence_guarded=false, the thinnest being sweeteners at relevant_count=7 against LowEvidenceThreshold=5, so the guard is inactive in every archived run. The corpus regression suite — TestCorpusBaseline, TestVerbGateCorrelation, TestKnownMisclassifications, TestTokenLeakage, TestDeterminism — passes with no DRIFT or STANCE MOVED marker on any logged line. The behavior is therefore pinned only by TestApplyLowEvidenceGuard, which covers both directional verdicts collapsing to insufficient-evidence, the exact-threshold boundary, the llm: bypass, an already-insufficient verdict as a no-op, and asserts bit-identical ConsensusScore/Confidence and NearUnanimous on every case. A one-off probe test that produced the zero-guarded-corpora count was deleted rather than kept, since it asserted nothing. NOT established: no live production run was re-executed after the change; the HPV observation above is the pre-change measurement.
